name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q01 - Non phagocytic cells among blood corpuscles

questiontext.text: Which of the following cells does not exhibit phagocytotic activity

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Phagocytosis is an essential cellular defense mechanism whereby specialized leukocytes engulf and digest foreign particles, microorganisms, and cellular debris.

Evaluation
Monocytes and neutrophils are circulating phagocytic white blood cells that actively ingest pathogens. Monocytes that exit the bloodstream and enter tissues differentiate into macrophages, which possess pronounced phagocytic capacity. In contrast, basophils are non-phagocytic granulocytes that function predominantly in inflammatory and allergic reactions by releasing biochemical mediators such as histamine, serotonin, and heparin.

Final Answer
Basophil does not exhibit phagocytic activity.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q02 - Common symptom in dengue fever infection

questiontext.text: One of the common symptoms observed in people infected with Dengue fever is

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Dengue fever is an acute mosquito-borne viral infection caused by the dengue virus and transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti.

Evaluation
A hallmark hematological manifestation of dengue infection is thrombocytopenia, which refers to a rapid and marked decline in blood platelet count. The virus suppresses bone marrow megakaryocytopoiesis and mediates immune destruction of circulating platelets, significantly heightening the risk of hemorrhage.

Final Answer
Significant decrease in platelets count.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q03 - Ventricular output during each cardiac cycle

questiontext.text: Which among the followings is correct during each cardiac cycle?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
During each cardiac cycle, the right and left ventricles contract to eject blood into the pulmonary and systemic circulations respectively. The volume pumped by each ventricle per beat is defined as the stroke volume (approximately \(70\text{ mL}\) in a resting adult).

Evaluation
Because the human circulatory system is organized into two circuits functioning in series, the pulmonary circulation and systemic circulation must handle equivalent volumetric flow rates over time. If one ventricle pumped a different volume of blood than the other, fluid would progressively accumulate in either the lungs or peripheral tissues, causing circulatory congestion. Therefore, the volume of blood pumped out by the right and left ventricles during each cardiac cycle is identical.

Final Answer
The volume of blood pumped out by the Rt and Lt ventricles is same.

answer.text: The volume of blood pumped out by the Rt and Lt ventricles is same.
The volume of blood pumped out by the Rt and Lt ventricles is different
The volume of blood received by each atrium is different
The volume of blood received by the aorta and pulmonary artery is different

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q04 - Autonomic neural regulation of cardiac activity

questiontext.text: Cardiac activity could be moderated by the autonomous neural system. Tick the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
The cardiovascular center in the medulla oblongata moderates cardiac activity through the autonomic nervous system via sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves.

Evaluation
Sympathetic stimulation releases noradrenaline, which acts on beta-1 adrenergic receptors in nodal tissues and ventricular myocardium. This increases the rate of depolarisation at the sinoatrial node, elevates heart rate, increases ventricular contractility, and elevates stroke volume, thereby raising cardiac output. In contrast, parasympathetic signals conveyed through the vagus nerve release acetylcholine to decrease heart rate and reduce cardiac output.

Final Answer
The sympathetic system stimulates heart rate and stroke volume.

answer.text: The parasympathetic system stimulates heart rate and stroke volume
The sympathetic system stimulates heart rate and stroke volume
The parasympathetic system decreases the heart rate but increases stroke volume
The sympathetic system decreases the heart rate but increases stroke volume

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q05 - Essential factors for blood coagulation process

questiontext.text: Mark the pair of substances among the following which is essential for coagulation of blood.

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Coagulation of blood is an enzymatic cascade mechanism that converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin polymers to form a hemostatic clot.

Evaluation
Upon vascular injury, disintegrated platelets release platelet factors that participate in the formation of the enzyme complex thrombokinase. Calcium ions (\(\text{Ca}^{2+}\)) are an indispensable cofactor (Factor IV) required at several enzymatic conversion steps, including the conversion of prothrombin to active thrombin and fibrin polymerization. Conversely, heparin is a physiological anticoagulant, while oxalates and citrates act as anticoagulants by chelating free calcium ions.

Final Answer
Calcium ions and platelet factors.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q06 - Unrepresented wave in standard electrocardiogram trace

questiontext.text: ECG depicts the depolarisation and repolarisation processes during the cardiac cycle. In the ECG of a normal healthy individual one of the following waves is not represented.

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
An electrocardiogram (ECG) records extracellular potential differences generated by cardiac muscle depolarization and repolarization across the cardiac cycle.

Evaluation
In a standard ECG tracing, atrial depolarization produces the P-wave, ventricular depolarization produces the QRS complex, and ventricular repolarization produces the T-wave. Atrial repolarization occurs simultaneously with ventricular depolarization; however, due to the large muscle mass of the ventricles, the electrical signal of ventricular depolarization completely masks the smaller atrial repolarization signal, leaving it unrepresented as an independent wave on a standard trace.

Final Answer
Repolarisation of atria.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q07 - Human blood cells lacking nucleus at maturity

questiontext.text: Which one of the following types of cells lack nucleus in humans?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
During maturation in the red bone marrow, human red blood corpuscles undergo specialized morphological adaptations to optimize gas transport efficiency.

Evaluation
Mature human erythrocytes (red blood cells) extrude their nuclei and lack other cellular organelles, which endows them with a biconcave disc shape and provides maximum internal space for packing hemoglobin molecules. In contrast, white blood cells such as neutrophils, eosinophils, and monocytes are nucleated cells that retain their nuclei throughout their functional life.

Final Answer
Erythrocytes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q08 - Specific blood cells producing humoral antibodies

questiontext.text: Which one of the following blood cells is involved in antibody production?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
The adaptive immune response comprises cell-mediated immunity and humoral (antibody-mediated) immunity carried out by specialized lymphocytes.

Evaluation
B-lymphocytes are responsible for humoral immunity. When exposed to their specific antigens, B-lymphocytes undergo clonal selection and differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells that synthesize soluble immunoglobulins. T-lymphocytes mediate cellular immunity and assist B cells, while red blood cells transport gases and neutrophils carry out phagocytosis.

Final Answer
B-Lymphocytes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q09 - Sequence of cardiac impulse conduction system

questiontext.text: The cardiac impulse is initiated and conducted further upto ventricle. The correct sequence of conduction of impulse is

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
The nodal musculature of the human heart possesses myogenic auto-excitability, generating and conducting action potentials along a precise anatomical pathway to coordinate chamber contractions.

Evaluation
The cardiac action potential is generated at the sinoatrial node (SA Node) situated in the upper right wall of the right atrium. The impulse propagates through the atrial wall to reach the atrioventricular node (AV Node) in the lower left corner of the right atrium. From the AV node, the wave of excitation enters the atrioventricular bundle (AV Bundle or Bundle of His), which divides into bundle branches along the interventricular septum, terminating in the extensive Purkinje fiber network throughout the ventricular myocardium.

Final Answer
S A Node A V Node A V Bundle Purkinje fiber.

answer.text: S A Node A V Node Purkinje fiber A V Bundle
S A Node Purkinje fiber A V Node A V Bundle
S A Node A V Node A V Bundle Purkinje fiber
S A Node Purkinje fiber A V Bundle A V Node

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q10 - Blood cells involved in inflammatory reactions

questiontext.text: The cells involved in inflammatory reactions are

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Inflammatory reactions are localized vascular and cellular responses to tissue damage or irritants, mediated by chemical secretions from specific blood cells.

Evaluation
Basophils constitute \(0.5\text{–}1\%\) of total leukocytes and contain coarse granules containing histamine, heparin, and serotonin. Release of these substances upon activation triggers local vasodilation and increased vascular permeability, directly mediating inflammatory reactions.

Final Answer
Basophils.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q11 - Valve closure producing second heart sound

questiontext.text: The second heart sound (dubb) is associated with the closure of

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Mechanical valve closure creates audible vibrations in the heart walls and major blood vessels that can be heard via a stethoscope.

Evaluation
The first heart sound (lubb) is produced by the closure of the atrioventricular valves (tricuspid and bicuspid) at the onset of ventricular systole. The second heart sound (dubb) is produced at the beginning of ventricular diastole when intraventricular pressure falls below arterial pressure, leading to the sharp closure of the semilunar valves (aortic and pulmonary valves) to prevent regurgitation of blood into the ventricles.

Final Answer
Semilunar valves.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q12 - Interpretation of events in standard electrocardiogram

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly explains a phase/ event in cardiac cycle in a standard electrocardiogram?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
Each wave and complex in an electrocardiogram corresponds to an electrical event that triggers a mechanical event during the cardiac cycle.

Evaluation
The P-wave denotes atrial depolarization, which leads to atrial contraction. The QRS complex represents the wave of depolarization spreading through the ventricles, which directly initiates and marks ventricular systole (ventricular contraction). The T-wave represents ventricular repolarization, while the interval between S and T corresponds to ventricular systole.

Final Answer
QRS complex indicates ventricular contraction.

answer.text: Time between S and T represents atrial systole.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q13 - ABO blood group designation criteria identification

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
The ABO blood grouping system is established on the basis of specific surface antigens present on red blood cells.

Evaluation
Blood groups are categorized according to the presence or absence of two surface carbohydrate antigens (antigen A and antigen B) on the membrane of erythrocytes, not by the antibodies in plasma. Blood group O individuals have no surface antigens on RBCs and naturally possess both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma. Blood group B blood cannot be transfused to blood group A individuals because recipient plasma contains anti-B antibodies that agglutinate donor erythrocytes. Blood group AB individuals have both antigens and lack plasma antibodies against ABO antigens, acting as universal recipients.

Final Answer
Blood group is designated on the basis of the presence of antibodies in the blood plasma.

answer.text: A person of 'O' blood group has anti 'A' and anti 'B' antibodies in his blood plasma.
A person of 'B' blood group can't donate blood to a person of 'A' blood group.
Blood group is designated on the basis of the presence of antibodies in the blood plasma.
A person of AB blood group is universal recipient.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q14 - Calculation of resting cardiac output value

questiontext.text: What would be the cardiac output of a person having 72 heart beats per minute and a stroke volume of 50 ml?

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions
Heart rate \(= 72\text{ beats/min}\)
Stroke volume \(= 50\text{ mL/beat}\)

Relevant Formulae and Principles
Cardiac output is defined as the volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle per minute:
\[\text{Cardiac Output} = \text{Stroke Volume} \times \text{Heart Rate}\]

Step-by-Step Working
Substituting the given quantities into the formula:
\[\text{Cardiac Output} = 50\text{ mL/beat} \times 72\text{ beats/min} = 3600\text{ mL/min}\]

Check and Final Answer
Multiplying \(50\) by \(72\) yields \(3600\text{ mL}\). The physiological value is fully consistent.
Final Answer: 3600 mL.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q15 - Matching circulatory system terms with functions

questiontext.text:
Match the terms given under Column 'A' with their functions given under Column 'B' and select the answer from the options given below:

Column IColumn II
A. Lymphatic Systemi. Carries oxygenated blood
B. Pulmonary veinii. Immune Response
C. Thrombocytesiii. To drain back the tissue fluid to the circulatory system
D. Lymphocytesiv. Coagulation of blood

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
The circulatory and lymphatic systems comprise cellular elements and specialized vessels that execute transport, fluid balance, hemostasis, and immune defense.

Evaluation
The lymphatic system absorbs interstitial tissue fluid and returns it to the venous circulatory system, while also absorbing dietary lipids from the intestine.
The pulmonary vein carries freshly oxygenated blood from the capillary beds of the lungs to the left atrium of the heart.
Thrombocytes (blood platelets) release clotting factors and initiate the blood coagulation cascade to prevent hemorrhage.
Lymphocytes (B cells and T cells) mediate adaptive immune responses through antibody secretion and cell-mediated cytotoxicity.
Consequently, the correct associations correspond to Lymphatic System matching the drainage of tissue fluid to the circulatory system, Pulmonary vein matching the carriage of oxygenated blood, Thrombocytes matching blood coagulation, and Lymphocytes matching the immune response.

Final Answer
A-iii, B-i, C-iv, D-ii.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q16 - Relationship between atrial filling and cardiac excitation

questiontext.text:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option

Statement 1 : Atria receive blood from all parts of the body which subsequently flows to ventricles.

Statement 2 : Action potential generated at sino-atrial node passes from atria to ventricles.

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
The cardiac cycle coordinates the mechanical flow of blood through cardiac chambers with the underlying generation and conduction of electrical impulses.

Evaluation
During cardiac diastole, venous return collects in the atria and passive filling of the ventricles begins. The sinoatrial node spontaneously fires an action potential that spreads through the atrial syncytium, inducing atrial systole to complete ventricular filling, before passing to the ventricles via the atrioventricular conduction pathway. The electrical excitation and the mechanical events of blood flow are intrinsically coupled and occur in a coordinated, synchronous manner throughout each cardiac cycle.

Final Answer
Action mentioned in Statements 1 and 2 are synchronous.

answer.text: Action mentioned in Statement 1 is dependent on action mentioned in Statement 2
Action mentioned in Statement 2 is dependent on action mentioned in Statement 1
Action mentioned in Statements 1 and 2 are independent of each other.
Action mentioned in Statements 1 and 2 are synchronous.
